GRADE 5 MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Time: 64 minutes

INSTRUCTIONS
1. Answer all questions.
2. Use neat handwriting.
2. For multiple choice, write the correct letter only.
3. For short answers, write clearly in the spaces provided.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A: Multiple Choice

1. About Whole Numbers at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

2. About Whole Numbers using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

3. About Whole Numbers when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. order numbers up to tens of thousands in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

5. About Addition at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. add up to three 6-digit numbers without regrouping up to a sum not exceeding 1,000,000 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Addition completely.
   C. Addition is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Addition.

6. About Addition using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. add up to two 6-digit numbers with double regrouping with the sum not exceeding 1,000, 000 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Addition completely.
   C. Addition is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Addition.

7. About Addition when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate sum by rounding off the addends to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Addition completely.
   C. Addition is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Addition.

9. About Subtraction at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. subtract up to two 6-digit numbers without regrouping in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Subtraction completely.
   C. Subtraction is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Subtraction.

10. About Subtraction using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. subtract of up to two 6-digit numbers with regrouping in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Subtraction completely.
   C. Subtraction is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Subtraction.

11. About Subtraction when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate difference by rounding off the minuend and subtrahend to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Subtraction completely.
   C. Subtraction is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Subtraction.

13. About Multiplication at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. multiply up to a 3-digit number by up to a 2-digit number in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication completely.
   C. Multiplication is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication.

14. About Multiplication using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate product by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication completely.
   C. Multiplication is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication.

15. About Multiplication when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. make patterns involving multiplication of numbers with product not exceeding 1000 in in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication completely.
   C. Multiplication is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication.

17. About Division at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. divide up to a 3-digit number by up to a 2-digit number where the dividend is greater than the divisor in real life,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

18. About Division using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. apply the relationship between multiplication and division in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

19. About Division when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. divide up to 3-digit number by 1000 in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

21. About Fractions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. simplify fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

22. About Fractions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. compare fractions in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

23. About Fractions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. order fractions with denominators not exceeding 12 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

25. About Decimals at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify place value of decimals up to thousandths in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

26. About Decimals using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. order decimals up to thousandths in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

27. About Decimals when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. add decimals up to thousandths in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

29. About Simple Equations at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. form simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Simple Equations completely.
   C. Simple Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Simple Equations.

30. About Simple Equations using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. solve simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Simple Equations completely.
   C. Simple Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Simple Equations.

31. About Simple Equations when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. form simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Simple Equations completely.
   C. Simple Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Simple Equations.

SECTION B: Short Answers

4. Give two examples of how you can use Whole Numbers at the market in your county.

8. Give two examples of how you can use Addition at the market in your county.

12. Give two examples of how you can use Subtraction at the market in your county.

16. Give two examples of how you can use Multiplication at the market in your county.

20. Give two examples of how you can use Division at the market in your county.

24. Give two examples of how you can use Fractions at the market in your county.

28. Give two examples of how you can use Decimals at the market in your county.

32. Give two examples of how you can use Simple Equations at the market in your county.
